title: Pyeongyeong
summary: The pyeongyeong is a court instrument of bent, L-shaped stone chimes hung in two rows from a painted frame. A player strikes each stone on its long arm with a horn mallet and it gives one clear, high note.
howToPlay: Eight stones are lit: four on the lower row, four on the upper row.
Strike the stone a closing ring marks, on its long arm.
Thick stones ring lower, thin stones higher. The notes are short and clear, so strike on time.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The round ends when the last stroke has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: All the stones are cut to the same shape and tuned by thickness, so the player sees a tidy row of notes. The frame is painted in the colours of a court hall.
credits: Tradition: the pyeongyeong of Korea; patterns written for this game
